concern: The inheritance column of gene_phenotype_seed.csv: one blank withheld (not filled), one value confirmed; no seed value changes.
why_this_is_load_bearing: `inheritance` reaches the user: `_lookup_gene_phenotype` ships it to the frontend as `inheritance_pattern`, beside the variant of the row's GENE. That is what makes an unevidenced value a per-gene claim rather than metadata, and it is why C1 is withheld. NOTE: an earlier revision also claimed a blank demoted the row in primary selection. That was wrong — selection keys on `annot.hpo_terms or annot.inheritance`, and the IL10 row already carries two HPO terms.

C1.verdict: WITHHELD — insufficient evidence for a per-gene claim.
C1.statement_considered: The IL10 row's inheritance is autosomal recessive (MONDO:0016542, 'IL10-related early-onset inflammatory bowel disease').
C1.outcome: No value is set. The row stays blank and is listed in _UNVERIFIED_BLANK_INHERITANCE as unverified (no inheritance mode asserted until the two-source gate is met) — explicitly NOT as polygenic, which was #2043's mis-classification.
C1.why_withheld: The row is gene-keyed. `_lookup_gene_phenotype` returns its value as the `inheritance_pattern` rendered beside an *IL10* variant, so it reads as a per-gene claim, not as ontology metadata about a disease entity. MONDO's synonyms for the term do include 'autosomal recessive early-onset inflammatory bowel disease', but that is one source, and the contract requires two agreeing sources that do not share an upstream assertion for a user-facing claim of this kind.
C1.search_performed: Three receptor cohorts were located and all characterise only the IL10RA/IL10RB RECEPTOR forms (not asserted to be independent of one another: PMID:19890111 and PMID:21519361 share an author, and nothing rests on their independence): PMID:19890111 (European consanguineous families), PMID:28267044 (42-patient Chinese survey) and PMID:21519361 (French cohort; IL10RA p.R262C, IL10RB p.E141X). Searches for an IL10 LIGAND loss-of-function cohort, each retained: Consensus (2026-08-31, 20 papers, derived record), Scite (2026-09-05/06, ligand-only term excluding the receptor genes, 17 records returned of a reported 22, derived record) and a PubMed ESearch (2026-09-06, Title/Abstract term excluding IL10RA/IL10RB, verbatim esearch + esummary retained). The Scite records were read at title level only (no abstracts retained): none of the 17 titles names an IL10 ligand cohort, and two congress-proceedings volumes cannot be classified from a title, so that search is recorded as surfacing no ligand cohort by title rather than as excluding one. The Consensus results (all 20 identities retained on 2026-09-06) contain Kotlarz 2012 and the GENIUS survey (Pigneur 2013); both are assessed under candidates_assessed. The PubMed ESearch returned exactly one record: PMID:22549091 (Kotlarz D et al., Gastroenterology 2012; 66 early-onset IBD patients, 3 with IL-10 mutations, homozygous loss of function). It is ONE source, and its author list shares 14 of 35 authors with PMID:19890111 (read from the retained eSummaries), so it cannot pair with that cohort as an independent second source. The one other cohort reporting IL10-mutant patients (Pigneur 2013) shares contributing-clinician authors with Kotlarz 2012, so the pair is not proven to be two cohorts. That is the whole supported statement about the literature.
C1.what_would_close_it: A second IL10 (ligand) loss-of-function cohort whose independence from PMID:22549091 is documented across all three dimensions the contract names -- no shared patients (cohort), no shared dataset, and a genotype-phenotype observation that does not derive from the other paper's assertion (upstream) -- author disjointness alone being necessary but not sufficient; or patient-level evidence that the IL10-mutant patients in PMID:24216686 are not those in PMID:22549091 plus the same dataset/upstream assessment; or a maintainer decision that the MONDO entity-level assertion is sufficient for a gene-keyed row. Filed as a scientific-validity issue.
C1.history: An earlier revision of this packet set the value on receptor-only evidence and claimed 'loss-of-function variants in IL10, IL10RA or IL10RB'. A later revision restated it at the entity level. Review established that the entity framing does not change what the software renders, so the value is now withheld outright.

candidates_assessed.note: Records surfaced by the retained searches that report IL10 (ligand) mutation carriers, assessed for whether they could form the two-independent-source pair the contract requires. None is cited in support of a claim; author lists were read from the retained eSummaries. All three are notice-checked the same way as the cited sources (PubMed EFetch typed relations and Scite metadata), because the cohort composition and author-overlap reading rest on them: none carries a correction, retraction, expression of concern or other editorial notice; PMID:22549091 carries two CommentIn (comment) relations, retained in its reduction.

C2.statement: VKORC1 coumarin (warfarin) resistance is autosomal dominant: heterozygous missense variants suffice. Nothing is asserted about VKORC1's other phenotypes (Rost 2004 also maps VKCFD2 families); an earlier revision stated VKCFD2's recessive mode and mechanism here on a single source and that half is withdrawn.
C2.drives: The VKORC1 row's existing 'Autosomal dominant' is UNCHANGED by this pull request, and the test that pins it guards against unintended drift of a pre-existing value; it is not a scientific confirmation. Two retained primary sources agree with the value, but cohort independence between them is not provable from the retained abstract-level records (see independence), so the two-independent-source gate is recorded as not established and the word 'confirmed' is withdrawn. #2043 asked for this row to be checked because it was the last survivor of #1959's AD-vs-AR observation.
C2.independence: Assessed across the three dimensions the contract names, from the retained eSummaries and the live abstracts (accessed 2026-09-06). Cohort: Rost 2004 reports the original warfarin-resistant kindreds and VKCFD2 families; Lewis 2016 reports a single patient carrying Val66Met studied twelve years later at a different institution. The retained records do not state or imply that this patient belongs to Rost's kindreds; that they are different individuals is not provable from abstract-level records, and is recorded as such. Dataset: separate -- Rost's linkage and sequencing versus Lewis's own patient genotype, clinical response and a homology model. Upstream assertion: the mapped claim is that a heterozygous missense variant suffices for coumarin resistance; Lewis's support for it is its own genotype-phenotype observation in that patient, and it relies on Rost only for VKORC1's identification as the gene, which is not the claim mapped here. Disjoint authors and a twelve-year gap are recorded as supporting, not sufficient, facts.
C2.note: The gene carries more than one phenotype in the literature, which is why the row needed confirming against its disease_name rather than pattern-matching off the gene symbol. This packet does not characterise the other phenotypes.

retraction_method: PubMed EFetch XML, read for typed CommentsCorrections relations (RefType), NOT publication type and NOT eLink. An original record keeps its own pubtype while corrections, errata and retractions are carried as separate linked records, so a pubtype scan is not a retraction check. The eLink `pubmed_pubmed*` link sets retained here are generic related-article neighbourhoods and do not expose the typed relation either -- an earlier revision of this packet treated their silence as clearance, which it is not. The typed check was run 2026-09-05 for all five cited PMIDs; the sanitized XML is the authority and raw/ncbi-pubmed-comments-corrections-derived.json is its reduction.
explicitly_not_claimed: No inheritance value in the seed is changed by this pull request: IL10 stays blank (withheld) and VKORC1 keeps 'Autosomal dominant'. #2043's item 3 — spot-checking the other 13 Mendelian rows against Monarch/OLS4 and correcting via gene_inheritance_overrides.json — is NOT done here and is filed separately: it needs a per-gene authoritative check, which is its own evidence exercise rather than a rider on this one. About the IL10 ligand literature, only the author-list overlaps recorded under claims.C1.candidates_assessed are asserted (read from retained eSummaries); no broader statement about who dominates that literature is made, and the supported search outcome is that no independent qualifying pair was established.

payload_integrity: Thirteen payloads are unedited verbatim API responses (four NCBI eSummary, two NCBI ESearch, five NCBI eLink, two EBI OLS4). Three payloads, the NCBI EFetch XML files for the five cited PMIDs, for PMID:22549091 and for the two candidate PMIDs, are SANITIZED: <Abstract> elements were removed under the bibliographic-metadata-only retention rule and nothing else was touched; each is labelled as such in its filename and in the derived record beside it. Six payloads are DERIVED records, labelled as such in the file itself: the Consensus call and the two Scite calls, none of which has an HTTP response to capture, and the three reductions of the EFetch XML files to their CommentsCorrections and publication-type fields. No payload required further sanitization: all are public bibliographic or ontology records with no genotype, sample, personal or credentialed data.
